telles1998.title: Does it matter who answers the race question? Racial classification and income inequality in Brazil
telles1998.summary: With a 1995 national survey that recorded both self- and interviewer-classification, estimated white-brown income gaps were larger under interviewer classification (26% vs 17% after controls), while black-brown gaps barely changed. Shows that who classifies matters, which bears on classification of a child by a parent versus by an enumerator.

schwartzman2007.title: Does money whiten? Intergenerational changes in racial classification in Brazil
schwartzman2007.summary: Using PNAD 2005, shows parents' classification of their children varies with parental education: more-educated nonwhite parents more often call their children white, both because they marry whites more and because their interracial couples label children white more often. The closest published analogue to the census parent-to-child classification question.
schwartzman2007.verification: verified: Crossref + abstract read (abstract truncated by Crossref at the 1996 comparison sentence)

carvalho2004.title: Estimating the stability of census-based racial/ethnic classifications: the case of Brazil
carvalho2004.summary: Proposes a way to estimate between-census category switching from cohort balances and applies it to colour categories in 1950-90. Finds a large deficit in the black category (about 38%) with a matching gain in brown, i.e. movement from preto to pardo between censuses.
carvalho2004.verification: verified: Crossref + abstract read (Illinois Experts page)

francis2012.title: Using Brazil's racial continuum to examine the short-term effects of affirmative action in higher education
francis2012.summary: Studies racial quotas at the University of Brasilia (2004). Quotas raised the share of black students and appear to have induced some people to misstate race, while others, especially the darkest-skinned, came to identify as black.
francis2012.verification: verified: Crossref + abstract read (via RePEc/IDEAS). Crossref also carries a duplicate DOI 10.1353/jhr.2012.0024.
francis2012.notes: Pre-dates Lei 12.711 (university-level quota, not the national law).

francis2013.title: Endogenous race in Brazil: affirmative action and the construction of racial identity among young adults
francis2013.summary: In university survey data, self-reported race depends on parents' race, family status, gender and the quota policy. Students of mixed-race families identify more with the mother's race than the father's, and men report lighter than women (conditional on skin tone). Directly relevant to mother-vs-father and gender patterns.

francistan2015.title: Inside the black box: affirmative action and the social construction of race in Brazil
francistan2015.summary: Follow-up of University of Brasilia entrants before and after quotas; finds a persistent shift in racial identification from non-black to black and from lighter to darker categories, consistent with state classification reshaping identity.
francistan2015.verification: verified: Crossref + abstract read via search-engine abstract copy (publisher page returned 403)

bailey2018.title: How states make race: new evidence from Brazil
bailey2018.summary: Compares 1995 and 2008 national surveys, before and after race-targeted affirmative action spread: lay racial self-identification increasingly uses the state's categories and matches government classification. Evidence that the policy changed how people declare.
bailey2018.verification: verified: Crossref + publisher page abstract read

freeman2025.title: The changing relationship between racial identity and skin color in Brazil
freeman2025.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
freeman2025.short_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
freeman2025.summary: With six LAPOP surveys (2010-2023) finds a darkening of self-identification net of interviewer-rated skin colour, medium and dark-skinned respondents increasingly identifying as Black, and light-skinned as Brown. Authors link this to Black consciousness and the extension of quotas to Brown and Black Brazilians; the non-White majority is mostly reclassification.
freeman2025.verification: verified: Crossref + abstract and introduction read (eScholarship copy)

marinho2019.title: Classificação de cor/raça de filhos em domicílios indígenas no Brasil
marinho2019.summary: With the 2010 census sample, studies how children of households with at least one Indigenous parent are classified (indigenous, pardo, white); socioeconomic status (income, maternal schooling) is associated with the colour/race assigned to the child. A census-based parent-to-child classification analysis.
marinho2019.notes: Crossref lists article id as e00006119 (page None).

tomas2025.title: Trends in interracial unions in Brazil between 2002 and 2022: anything new?
tomas2025.journal: Revista Brasileira de Estudos de População
tomas2025.short_journal: Revista Brasileira de Estudos de População
tomas2025.summary: PNAD 2002-2022 show interracial unions stable at about 30% with no upward trend, but rising brown and black homogamy; regional differences reflect local racial distribution. Gives the share of children potentially exposed to mixed-parent classification.
tomas2025.notes: Author initials from Crossref ('M Tomas'); confirm before citing. Pages as listed by Crossref (1-12), probably an e-locator.

marteleto2012.title: Educational inequality by race in Brazil, 1982-2007: structural changes and shifts in racial classification
marteleto2012.summary: PNAD 1982-2007: the black-pardo gap in schooling narrowed, and the author finds evidence that both structural change and shifts in racial classification contribute. Documents that classification changes alter measured inequalities.

travassos2011.title: Comparison between two race/skin color classifications in relation to health-related outcomes in Brazil
travassos2011.journal: International Journal for Equity in Health
travassos2011.short_journal: International Journal for Equity in Health
travassos2011.summary: World Health Survey Brazil 2003 (n=5000): on a 1-10 skin-colour scale women classified themselves slightly lighter than men, an effect absent with IBGE categories; respondents tend to choose central shades. Supports the gender-and-colour point with a caveat about the instrument.

telles2004.title: Race in another America: the significance of skin color in Brazil
telles2004.summary: Book-length study of Brazilian racial classification, inequality and sociability using the 1991 census and PERS survey; reports that most marriages (77% in 1991) are colour-endogamous and that interviewer skin-colour ratings matter more than self-identification for inequality. Standard framing reference.
telles2004.verification: partial: DOI resolves in Crossref; no abstract in Crossref. Summary from publisher/review snippets (Project MUSE, Princeton), not from the book text.

lei12711.title: Lei n. 12.711, de 29 de agosto de 2012: dispoe sobre o ingresso nas universidades federais e nas instituicoes federais de ensino tecnico de nivel medio
lei12711.summary: Federal quota law: at least 50% of places in federal higher-education institutions reserved for public-school students, with sub-quotas for self-declared pretos, pardos and indigenous people (statute text; sub-quota detail beyond article 1 not re-read). Establishes the incentive structure behind post-2012 declaration changes.

ibge2013.title: Caracteristicas etnico-raciais da populacao: classificacoes e identidades (Estudos e Analises, Informacao Demografica e Socioeconomica, n. 2)
ibge2013.summary: Reports IBGE's 2008 PCERP pilot on how people classify themselves and others (self-identification versus hetero-classification, open versus closed colour questions, multiple answers). Grey literature on the instrument; I did not find in it an analysis of parents classifying children.

soaresfilho2011.title: Vitimização por homicídios segundo características de raça no Brasil
soaresfilho2011.summary: Time series of homicide in Brazil 2000-2009 from SIM: the black population made up 69% of victims in 2009; homicide numbers and rates rose among black people while falling among white people, with differences by schooling.
soaresfilho2011.verification: verified: Crossref + abstract read (abstract truncated by Crossref)

cerqueira2014.title: Vidas perdidas e racismo no Brasil
cerqueira2014.summary: Analyses violent lethality of black and non-black people by state, estimates lost life expectancy at birth due to violence, and tests whether the gap persists after socioeconomic controls (racism cannot be excluded). Uses SIM; defines negro as preto+pardo.
cerqueira2014.verification: verified: PDF read (title page and abstract). Crossref pages say 79-90 but the article prints 73-90 in the journal header; used 73-90.

aiquoc2022.title: Gender and race inequalities in adolescent and young adult homicide mortality rates: a multilevel analysis
aiquoc2022.summary: Ecological multilevel study of homicide rates at ages 15-29 by sex and race in Brazilian municipalities, 2015-2017 (SIM + Census); finds racial inequality in homicide mortality related to municipal factors such as adult violence and education/social-protection inequalities.

romero2019.title: Tendência e desigualdade na completude da informação sobre raça/cor dos óbitos de idosos no Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade, Brasil, 2000-2015
romero2019.summary: SIM race/colour completeness for deaths of older adults 2000-2015 is high nationally, with lower completeness in small and Northeastern municipalities; authors conclude the field is adequate for inequality studies except at some municipal levels. Not specific to external causes or young ages.
romero2019.verification: verified: Crossref + abstract read; conclusion from search-engine abstract copy

barbosa2023.title: Assessment of incompleteness of Mortality Information System records on deaths from external causes in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, 2000-2019
barbosa2023.summary: 146,882 external-cause deaths in Rio Grande do Sul: incompleteness of sex, age and place was very low and race/colour incompleteness showed a stable trend (below 5% in the period according to a summary of the full text), while schooling and marital status were worse.

melo2015.title: Incompletude dos registros de óbitos por causas externas no Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade em Pernambuco, Brasil, 2000-2002 e 2008-2010
melo2015.summary: Pernambuco external-cause deaths: race/colour incompleteness fell by about 54% between 2000-2002 and 2008-2010 while schooling, medical assistance and necropsy fields stayed highly incomplete.

barros2002.title: Validação de variáveis de declarações de óbito por causas externas, Recife, PE, Brasil
barros2002.summary: Compares death-certificate variables for external-cause deaths under age 20 in Recife (1995) against Instituto de Medicina Legal records: agreement was excellent or good for variables the legists see as their direct responsibility (sex, age, type of violence), and poorer for those they see as indirect or not theirs. Whether race/colour was among the poorer ones was not confirmed from the truncated abstract.

santos2013.title: Identificação racial e a produção da informação em saúde
santos2013.summary: Interviews and observation at the Salvador IML (2007): race/colour of bodies is omitted or assigned imprecisely because self-declaration is impossible; pretos and pardos are lumped as 'faiodermas', and the identification process distorts the final death-certificate information. Direct evidence on who assigns race at violent deaths.
santos2013.notes: Crossref gives pages 341-356; the article prints 341-55.

rodrigues2012.title: Desimportância da raça/cor e responsabilidade médico-legal no preenchimento da declaração de óbito
rodrigues2012.summary: Interviews at the IML of Feira de Santana (Bahia): the legists value the death certificate but attend mostly to the cause of death; since the dead cannot self-declare, the legist defines the victim's race/colour, which they treat as of little importance.
rodrigues2012.verification: partial: Crossref + abstract read (truncated); page field is a single value (884), real range unverified; Crossref dates it 2012 although the volume is 35 (2011)
rodrigues2012.notes: Crossref family/given fields look inverted for these authors (e.g. 'Castro Rodrigues' as family name); initials here are my reconstruction, verify on the journal page before citing.

melo2013.title: Produção da informação sobre mortalidade por causas externas: sentidos e significados no preenchimento da Declaração de Óbito
melo2013.summary: Qualitative interviews with physicians show the death certificate carries different meanings (epidemiological vs legal) depending on how death occurred, so data production is not neutral or purely technical. Context for how violent-death certificates are completed.

chipperfield2015.title: Using the bootstrap to account for linkage errors when analysing probabilistically linked categorical data

Still requires the linkage process to be replicable on record-level files.

lahiri2005.journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association
lahiri2005.short_journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association
lahiri2005.summary: Linear-regression estimator that removes the bias caused by false matches, given known probabilities that record pairs are true links, with a bootstrap for linkage-model uncertainty. Does not handle 1-1 linkage.
